component.name: Solander
component.summary: Read your Markdown vault in place, without ever writing into it

description.p: A reading application that opens a folder of Markdown straight from disk and renders it as itself, fluent in Obsidian's dialect: wikilinks, embeds, callouts, frontmatter, tags, highlights, canvases, kanban boards and Dataview queries.

Nothing is ever written into the vault, no plugin or script ever executes, and the network is never touched. A solander is the clamshell box an archive keeps its documents in: the job is to present the record and leave it exactly as it was found.

The same note in Blood Record, one of the thirteen Archive themes

description.p: Frontmatter in notes saved with Windows line endings is recognized again, so a note's title, tags and CSS classes no longer appear as body text.

Fixes a Flatpak that would not start. The check deciding whether the renderer's sandbox can run cannot succeed inside Flatpak and does not need to, because Flatpak is itself the sandbox. Also corrects the version the application reports.

Corrects the application metadata a software centre reads: this listing had no screenshots, links or keywords, and did not validate. The install documentation now leads with the packaged installs and says that the Flatpak bundle needs the GNOME runtime it does not contain. Every continuous-integration action is pinned to a commit.
Debian and Flatpak packages, built and published automatically when a version is tagged.
Documentation pass: the name explained, screenshots, and a contributing guide.
--sandbox prints the AppArmor profile this installation needs; --sandbox-status reports whether it is installed, attached and working.
The application mark sits on its own tile, so it carries the same visual weight as the icons beside it.
The application mark fills its canvas, so it no longer reads as half-size beside other icons in a dock.
The window carries its own icon: the process now identifies itself by app id, and the installer refreshes the icon theme cache.
Obsidian Reader is now Solander. Same application, same Obsidian compatibility; your session and indexes are adopted automatically.
Thirteen dark themes in the Archive family, sharing one design language, with every text colour measured against WCAG AA.
A new application mark: a sealed archival plate on a plinth, with a seal set into a diamond cut, in both themes.
A second theme: Blood Record, a dark archive in charcoal, bone and blood, chosen under Appearance. The original Atelier theme is unchanged.
The page indicator gets its own strip, pages keep a book measure on large screens, and the desk paints opaquely behind the page.
Book mode turns real pages: chapters are paginated by WebKit's print pipeline and turned page by page — no scrolling at all.
Book mode: read a folder of chapters as a book — page-turn transitions, chapter navigation, remembered progress, and the book's own vault stylesheet and fonts.
Mermaid flowcharts, sequence diagrams, and pies render as static SVG, drawn in pure Python — no JavaScript involved.
The outline lives in the right panel only; the sidebar page is removed.
The outline shows on one side at a time — left rail page or right panel, chosen in the View menu — and the rail version gets its own treatment with a heading hierarchy.
Sidebar structure: a collapsible pinned-and-recent section, a labeled folder tree, an outline page in the rail, and tag and graph icons that actually show on the dark surface.
The outline panel joins the visual identity: a warm card surface, gold label, and serif entries.
Two surfaces instead of one tint: a full-height sepia rail beside the parchment canvas, a flattened header, and a note title that never doubles.
The outline becomes a real panel with a visible toggle and close button, the header bar is simplified, and every surface in the app has an obvious control.

The atelier redesign: a manuscript identity across the whole app — warm palettes shared by chrome and canvas, serif display type, a real welcome page, and every note-context element individually toggleable.
An editorial redesign of the reading surface: note headers with breadcrumb and metadata, an on-this-page rail, linked mentions after the content, and pinned notes in the sidebar.
A guided setup window replaces the terminal-only sandbox step, and the user guide and getting-started docs open inside the app.
The mind map carries a visible way back, and Ctrl+M toggles between a note and its map.
Hide folders from the tree and search, and view any note as a mind map of its headings and bullets.
Kanban boards, Excalidraw drawings, and sanitized vault CSS snippets — the reader now renders every content type a working vault contains.
Dataview queries, inline expressions, and .base table views evaluate in pure Python — live, sanitized, and with honest degradation for anything unsupported.
PDF export no longer splits boxes across pages or clips wide code and tables; exports print light with dark ink.
Embedded PDF preview through system Poppler, with zoom and an external-open fallback when the bindings are absent.
TeX math as native MathML, canvas files rendered as static pages, and typography controls for font, line width, and spacing.
Fuzzy quick-open with recent notes, highlighted search hits, a native local-graph pane, and a fix for a garbage-collector crash.

The live layer: a persistent per-vault index makes launches near-instant, file monitors keep the tree, search, and link graph current as the vault changes, and full-text search is ranked by relevance.
Backlinks with context, a tag browser, the vault's bookmarks, search operators (path:, file:, tag:), and hover previews of linked notes.
Tabs with middle-click and Ctrl+click to open notes and links in them, a resizable sidebar, and single-click folder expansion.
The launcher execs the interpreter directly so the AppArmor sandbox profile actually attaches; shebang launches bypassed it.
Detects Ubuntu's user-namespace restriction before WebKit's sandbox crashes on it, and prints the AppArmor profile that fixes it.
Reading (zen) mode and PDF export of the rendered note, which refuses to write inside the vault.
First release: vault browsing, Obsidian Markdown rendering, link resolution with disambiguation, embeds with cycle detection, search, session restore, and a hardened no-script rendering surface.
